thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Nasdaq Futures Climb, Led Higher By Apple's Jump

author: www.4-traders.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Nasdaq Futures Climb, Led Higher By Apple's Jump
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch
Futures for the Dow industrials, S&P 500 show little change
Futures for the Nasdaq-100 index gained ground early Wednesday, boosted by Apple Inc.'s earnings-driven jump in premarket trading.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 looked set for more muted moves, as traders braced for a Federal Reserve policy statement, as well as ADP's monthly report on private-sector employment.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
Nasdaq-100 futures rose by 29.50 points, or 0.4%, to 6,721.50.
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures traded roughly flat at 24,075, while S&P 500 futures gained 4.05 points, or 0.2%, to 2,656.25.
On Tuesday, the Dow finished 0.3% lower , while the S&P 500 advanced by 0.3% and the tech-laden Nasdaq Composite rose 0.9%.
The Dow and S&P are down 2.5% and 0.7% for the year, as of Tuesday's close. The Nasdaq Composite has climbed 3.3%.
What's driving markets?
Apple's stock (AAPL)rose 3.4% in premarket action after the largest American company by market capitalization late Tuesday posted better-than-anticipated earnings and revenue for the first quarter.
Check out:Apple earnings were saved by the company's new MVP
Encouraging first-quarter earnings from many companies have helped the main equity benchmarks rally in recent weeks, though investors also have been worried about protectionism and other geopolitical flare-ups.
Which economic releases are on tap?
Fed officials are due to wrap up a two-day meeting, and the policy makers are expected to leave interest rates on hold and signal no change to a tightening path of two more rate increases in 2018.
The Federal Open Market Committee's policy statement is slated to hit at 2 p.m. Eastern Time.
Don't miss: Why the Fed could make 4 rate hikes this year
ADP's April release on private-sector employment is expected to arrive at 8:15 a.m. Eastern. It typically serves as a preview to Friday's more closely watched jobs report from the U.S. government, also known as the monthly nonfarm payrolls data.
